repositories.name: kmeans-demo
repositories.description: k-Means für die Standortwahl von Depots – Verfolgen Sie Lloyd's Algorithmus Iteration für Iteration: Zuweisung und Zentren-Update wechseln sich ab, bis die Zielfunktion konvergiert. Interaktive Streamlit-Demo, Teil von sebastianhanisch.net

paragraphs: Zweites Stück der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning" (nach branch-bound-demo): anders als die Fall-Demos im Portfolio (ein Anwendungsfall, mehrere Verfahren im Vergleich) zeigt diese Demo ein Verfahren – k-Means (Lloyd's Algorithmus) – und lässt stattdessen die Optimierungslandschaft wachsen. Vehikel-Problem: Kundenstandorte auf k Depots aufteilen, jedes Depot bedient die ihm am nächsten liegenden Kunden – die Summe der quadrierten Entfernungen zu minimieren ist exakt die k-Means-Zielfunktion.

Die Konzepte-Reihe ist kein linearer Pfad, sondern mehrere unabhängige Linien: diese Demo ist der Startpunkt einer eigenen Clustering-Linie, unabhängig von branch-bound-demos Exakte-Suche-Linie - und verzweigt sich hier in zwei unabhängige Äste:

Ein Ast behebt k-Means' dichte-/verbindungsbasierte Schwächen: dbscan-demo (k muss nicht vorab feststehen, Cluster müssen nicht konvex/kugelförmig sein) und, davon unabhängig, agglomerative-demo (Chaining bei Single-Linkage) - beide laufen auf hdbscan-demo zu, das live nachweist, dass HDBSCAN beide Probleme löst. Ein zweiter, unabhängiger Ast behebt eine ANDERE Schwäche - die implizite Annahme kugelförmiger, gleich gestreuter Cluster und harter Zuweisung: gmm-demo (Gaussian Mixture Models, EM-Algorithmus), bei dem k-Means selbst der Grenzfall ist, fortgesetzt von dpmm-demo…

repositories.name: mcts-demo
repositories.description: Monte Carlo Tree Search auf demselben Netz – Sehen Sie, wie zufällige Rollouts und UCB1 die handgemachte Heuristik ersetzen. Mit wachsendem Raster kollabiert der spärliche Reward. Interaktive Streamlit-Demo, Teil von sebastianhanisch.net

paragraphs: Achtes und letztes Stück der Heuristische-Baumsuche-Linie der "Konzepte"-Reihe für die Website "Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning". Alle sieben Stücke davor (greedy-best-first-demo, astar-demo, ida-star-demo, beam-search-demo, monobeam-demo, beam-stack-demo, diverse-beam-demo) teilen eine Annahme: es gibt eine handgemachte Heuristik h(n), hier die Luftlinie zum Ziel. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS, hier UCT: Kocsis & Szepesvári 2006) ersetzt sie durch zufällige Rollouts: den Wert eines Knotens schätzt es, indem es von dort einen Zufallslauf bis zum Ziel simuliert;…

Einordnung in die Linie: MCTS ist ein unabhängiger Ast der Wurzel (keine Fortsetzung von Beam Search oder A\). Derselbe Graph und dieselben Instanzen wie in den Geschwistern (die Suchkerne search, greedybestfirst, uniformcostsearch, astar sind wortgleich kopiert und reproduzieren deren Zahlen, als Test hinterlegt); Uniform-Cost (das Optimum ohne Heuristik - die ehrliche Basis), A\ und Greedy Best-First dienen als Vergleichsgrößen. Neu ist mctssearch und Zufall im Kern (Seed des Laufs als Regler).

Ergebnis in Kürze: Ohne Heuristik findet MCTS Routen, aber schlechte und teuer. Auf dem Standardraster (Größe 12, 15 % Hindernisse, 4000 Iterationen) findet reines MCTS in 100 % der Läufe eine Route - in keinem Lauf die optimale und im Median 17.1 % über dem Optimum; Uniform-Cost findet das Optimum mit 121 Expansionen, MCTS braucht im Median rund 81 000 Knotenbesuche (andere Einheit, aber Größenordnungen). Mit wachsendem Raster kollabiert der spärliche Reward (Ziel-Rollouts 95 % bei Größe 6, 0.2 % bei Größe 22; Lücke bis 68 %). Und der Erfolg gehört zum großen Teil nicht MCTS: mit einem durch…

repositories.description: Warehouse Management System (ASP.NET Core 9, React, PostgreSQL): receiving, picking, packing, shipping, roles. Try it in the browser with no server (fictional data) or with one docker compose command.

paragraphs: A full-stack Warehouse Management System for a distribution center. It covers the whole physical cycle: receiving and put-away, stock control, order allocation, picking, packing, shipping, adjustments, transfers and returns, with role-based access and a REST API documented in Swagger.
Portfolio case study. A personal project built to practise designing a realistic WMS domain model, API and UI. It is not affiliated with any company and ships with fictional demo data only.

Distribution centers live and die by inventory accuracy. This project models the inbound-to-outbound flow end to end so the business rules are explicit and tested: stock only changes through traceable ledger transactions, allocation cannot over-reserve, picking cannot exceed what was requested, shipping requires packing, and corrections need a second person's approval.
features: Inbound: planned receipts with lines, receiving with put-away to a location in one step (repeatable, only the delta posts), damaged goods recorded but not stocked, lot-mixing protection, receipt completion as Received…

Outbound: orders with lines, all-or-nothing stock allocation (first-expiry-first-out, fullest bin first), pick tasks per bin, pick confirmation with over-pick rejection and short picks, packing into cartons, shipping…

Inventory: per-bin on-hand/reserved/available, an immutable movement ledger (inbound, outbound, adjustment, transfer, return), adjustments (increase, decrease, recount) that apply only after approval and are…
Safety: optimistic concurrency token on every stock row so two simultaneous allocations cannot both win, and consistent 400/403/404/409 error messages the UI shows verbatim.
Master data: warehouses, zones, locations, products, categories, units of measure, suppliers, carriers.

whatItDoes.text: A full-stack Warehouse Management System for a distribution center. It covers the whole physical cycle: receiving and put-away, stock control, order allocation, picking, packing, shipping, adjustments, transfers and returns, with role-based access and a REST API documented in Swagger.

repositories.name: mobile-tabs
repositories.description: Vue demo of a sliding tab animation on mobile. Made with svg and gsap.

paragraphs: This is a simple Vue demo to explore an idea of sliding tab navigation. I used svg to create the curved shape and gsap to do the animation.

The trick is simple: with a white bottom navbar and a grey background (replace with your colors), I just need to place a svg path with the curved shape right on top (width equal to 1/4 or 1/ as many items as your navbar holds), filled with the color of the background behind the navbar. This way, you have a nice curved "hole" you just need to translate between the nav items to give a smooth sliding effect.

I just added the ball as another svg element, and used a gsap timeline to make it go down then up during tab change. The enter-leave animation for the slides/pages are a basic vue transition with v-if and the tab data coupled with a css transition declaration on relevant classes.

whatItDoes.text: This is a simple Vue demo to explore an idea of sliding tab navigation. I used svg to create the curved shape and gsap to do the animation.

Broken Arrow gives you real vehicles, real weapons and real doctrine, and then lets a 152 mm howitzer drop a shell on the tank parked next to it, lets a machine gun swat an aircraft three kilometres up, and caps every missile at the 9 km edge of its old maps.

You will escort your transports, because when a carrier is destroyed, the squads inside rarely get out.
You will stop using artillery as a panic button, because guns have minimum ranges, real aiming times and a real emplacement after every move.
You will fear the ground when you fly, because two anti-air missile hits bring down anything that flies, and flying low hands you to every machine gun in reach.

repositories.name: outbox
repositories.description: Implements the Transactional Outbox pattern. Persists domain events atomically with aggregate state changes through a customizable table schema, reflection-based payload serialization, and built-in support for event schema versioning.

paragraphs: The Transactional Outbox pattern solves the dual-write problem: persisting an aggregate state change and publishing an integration event must happen atomically. Doing both independently risks a crash leaving one side committed and the other lost. The outbox pattern records both in the same database transaction, delegating event delivery to a separate relay process.

This library is the write-side adapter. It persists every domain fact atomically with aggregate state via Doctrine DBAL. Domain events with a registered translator follow the pipeline DomainEvent → IntegrationEventTranslator → IntegrationEvent → PayloadSerializer → INSERT and are persisted as integration events. Domain events without a translator are persisted as well, carrying the domain event itself: the row takes the domain event's own type and revision, and its payload is produced by reflection over the event's public properties. Every record produces a row, so the unique constraint over…

The library is opinionated on correctness: transactions are always required, JSON validity is always checked, and every schema decision is left to you: table name, column names, and identity column storage type are all configurable.

paragraphs: A small, opinionated React design system that ships with machine-readable specs for every component. Built so AI agents (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, MCP servers) can read the contract, validate against it, and extend the system without hallucinating tokens or breaking accessibility.

Most design systems ship code + Storybook and hope documentation keeps up. This one ships a third artifact — /specs// — that an agent can load and treat as the source of truth. See AGENTS.md for the contract, and AI-READY-ARCHITECTURE.md for the 9-tray AI-ready roadmap (foundations → components → AI surfaces → behavior → trust → eval loop).
When an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, an MCP server) is asked to build a screen using this system, the failure modes are predictable:
features: Invents tokens that don't exist (color.brand.primary)
Misses required ARIA (focus ring, aria-busy on loading)
Skips an interaction state (focus, disabled, loading)
Picks the wrong variant for the context
Closed token list — specs//tokens.json is the complete set of tokens that component may use. Anything else is a lint failure.

repositories.description: Extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements, based on the MASS framework

paragraphs: Extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements.

Music generates and manipulates sound in LPCM audio, sample by sample. It implements MASS (Music and Audio in Sample Sequences), a collection of psychophysical descriptions of musical elements expressed as equations and corresponding Python routines.

The adsr is not decoration. A note ends wherever its phase lands and the next one opens at the bottom of its wavetable, so concatenating them raw steps -- by up to the full scale, and on nine of this scale's twelve joins. An envelope runs each note to silence at both ends, which is what makes the joins joins rather than clicks.

features: Plain synchronous handlers. No async def, event loop, or coroutine bridge.
Compiled endpoint plans. Route matching metadata, argument sources, path conversions,
Interpreter-adaptive scheduling. With the GIL disabled, one process uses a real thread
msgspec request bodies. JSON decoding and validation happen together in compiled C
Optional Rust/PyO3 request-head parser. A compatible dexpot-native installation

paragraphs: "Automatically open a PR on your Git repository when a file update is needed"

Updatecli is a universal declarative update policy engine. Designed to be used from everywhere, each Updatecli "run" detects if a file needs to be updated using a tailored update policy then apply changes.
You describe your update strategy in a policy then you enforce it using Updatecli.
features: Sources — Fetch the new value to apply (e.g. latest Docker image tag, newest Helm chart version, latest GitHub release).
Conditions — Verify that all prerequisites are met before making any change (optional but recommended).
Targets — Apply the change to the right file or service, and open a pull request if an SCM is configured.
Declarative — Define your update policy once in YAML; Updatecli handles detection and application.
30+ integrations — Docker, Helm, GitHub releases, npm, PyPI, Terraform, AWS AMIs, and more — out of the box.

repositories.description: AI-powered recipe generator using Google Gemini Vision, LangChain & Streamlit. Scan a photo of your fridge or pantry, edit the detected ingredients, and chat with a ReAct Chef agent for custom recipes by flavor, cooking method & diet. English & Indonesian.

paragraphs: Chef AI is an intelligent recipe generator that turns your available ingredients into delicious meals. Powered by Google Gemini Vision and LangChain, this application allows users to upload photos of their fridge or pantry, automatically detects ingredients, and generates tailored recipes based on specific dietary preferences, cooking methods, and flavor profiles.
Whether you are a beginner looking for a quick meal or a home cook wanting to try something new, Chef AI adapts to your needs using dynamic prompt engineering and agentic reasoning.

Under the hood, the app is a two-phase pipeline wrapped in a single Streamlit interface. Phase 1 uses Gemini's multimodal vision to read a photo and produce an editable ingredient list. Phase 2 feeds that list, together with the user's preferences, into a LangChain ReAct agent that writes the recipe and keeps chatting with you to refine it. The interface is available in both English and Indonesian, and every recipe can be downloaded as a .txt file.
features: Snap & Scan: Upload an image or take a photo directly via the app.
Auto-Listing: The AI identifies ingredients and lists them in a bulleted format.
Manual Override: Users can edit the detected list to fix typos or add missing items.
Supported Formats: jpg, jpeg, png, and webp uploads, plus live camera capture (the camera is opt-in through a checkbox, so it is never switched on by default).
Strict Output Format: The detection prompt asks for a bulleted list only, with no introduction or closing remarks.

repositories.name: IndoorKit
repositories.description: Indoor map SDK built from scratch on MapLibre GL JS + TypeScript, with a hospital RTLS demo: real-time tracking, assets, alerts, occupancy heatmap.

paragraphs: IndoorKit is an indoor mapping SDK for the browser, written in TypeScript on top of MapLibre GL JS. It reads venues in IMDF, draws floors and rooms in 2.5D, and puts everything else (floors, markers, live positions, geofences, heatmaps, routes) into plugins that are typed end to end and clean up after themselves.
features: Plugin system. definePlugin declares a plugin and its dependencies. Plugins load in dependency order, and their APIs are typed on indoor.plugins.

No leaks by design. Every source, layer, listener, timer and Worker a plugin creates is registered with a ResourceTracker, and destroy() releases them in reverse order. A memory regression test checks the JS heap,…
Styles from data. Room colors and heights come from the room category and a theme, and rooms and walls are extruded without 3D models. Language and theme switch at runtime without recreating the map.

Real-time positioning. A DataProvider contract for location feeds, with a position stream that interpolates thousands of tags smoothly, plus trails with stop detection, geofences, room clustering and bounded-memory…
Business logic stays outside. The SDK knows nothing about any industry. Domain packages hold the rules and do not depend on the map or the DOM.

whatItDoes.text: IndoorKit is an indoor mapping SDK for the browser, written in TypeScript on top of MapLibre GL JS. It reads venues in IMDF, draws floors and rooms in 2.5D, and puts everything else (floors, markers, live positions, geofences, heatmaps, routes) into plugins that are typed end to end and clean up after themselves.

paragraphs: Zero-infrastructure remote laptop control from your phone, from anywhere.

TetherDesk lets you view and control your laptop screen from your phone across any network — different Wi-Fi, different carrier, different country. No server to maintain, no monthly subscription, no app store installation required.

paragraphs: A content-based movie recommender using TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity, built with Python and scikit-learn, and deployed as a live Streamlit web app.

This project builds a content-based recommendation system that suggests movies similar to one a user already likes. Instead of relying on other users' ratings (collaborative filtering), it compares movies directly based on their content — genre, keywords, tagline, cast, and director — using TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity. The final model is deployed as an interactive Streamlit web app where a user types a movie name and instantly receives a ranked list of similar titles.

whatItDoes.text: A content-based movie recommender using TF-IDF vectorization and cosine similarity, built with Python and scikit-learn, and deployed as a live Streamlit web app.

repositories.name: investment-crossover-point-calculator
repositories.description: A privacy-friendly browser calculator for investment growth crossover and financial independence milestones.

paragraphs: Investment Crossover Point Calculator is a free, privacy-friendly, browser-based financial planning tool that helps users explore two different investment milestones that are often described with the same phrase. The first milestone is the growth crossover point, when projected annual investment growth becomes equal to or greater than the amount contributed during that year. The second milestone is the financial independence crossover point, when projected annual portfolio spending, based on a selected planning withdrawal rate, becomes equal to or greater than inflation-adjusted annual…

The project separates these milestones because they answer different questions. Growth crossover helps users understand when compounding may become a larger annual contributor than new savings. Financial independence crossover helps users estimate when a portfolio may support a chosen level of annual spending. A later growth crossover does not automatically mean weaker financial progress. Higher contributions can raise the crossover threshold while also building a larger portfolio and bringing the financial independence milestone closer.

This website is designed as a lightweight static application. It requires no account, no database, no server-side calculation, and no build process. All calculations run locally in the browser. The project can be hosted directly on GitHub Pages or any standard static web server.

paragraphs: ProbAge is a Python package implementing the probabilistic model for epigenetic age acceleration analysis described in "Probabilistic inference of epigenetic age acceleration from cellular dynamics" (Nature Aging, 2024). This tool provides a mechanistic approach to understanding methylation dynamics and biological aging, addressing limitations in traditional epigenetic clock methods.
features: Probabilistic modeling of methylation transitions at the cellular level
Distinction between acceleration and bias components in methylation dynamics
Robust inference framework tested on large-scale cohort data
Compatible with both local execution and cloud-based analysis
